arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case assert the Eleventh Circuit wrongly banned Rule 60(b) in habeas cases.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of Rule 60(b) in federal habeas proceedings. the sides that brought the case argue the rule allows courts to correct certain errors. the opposing sides claim the rule is categorically unavailable in habeas cases.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines the tools available to correct federal habeas errors. It shapes how courts handle procedural mistakes in prisoner litigation. The outcome clarifies the boundary between habeas and civil procedure rules.
